writing.exampleCaption: entry inserts a default only when the key is missing.
writing.explanation: Choosing a collection is part of the model, not an afterthought: order, uniqueness, and key access all change what your code can promise. Each of these owns its data, so passing one around follows exactly the same ownership rules as any other value.
writing.feedback: entry avoids a second lookup and the borrow conflict that comes with it.
writing.practiceCode:
let mut map = HashMap::new();
map.insert("a", map.get("a").unwrap_or(&0) + 1);
writing.question: Why is entry() better here?
writing.rule: entry().or_insert() gives you a mutable reference either way.
